name: Gole Hatti
short_description: Legendary 1954 seated dhaba on Khari Baoli Road famous for serving Palak Chole Chawal in earthen kulhads and fluffy bhaturas.
long_description: Established in 1954 at Fatehpuri Chowk near the entrance of Khari Baoli, Gole Hatti is a beloved culinary landmark for pure vegetarian Old Delhi comfort fare. The historic, bustling dining hall features indoor table service where patrons gather for its signature Chole Palak Chawal served in earthen clay kulhads, accompanied by onion pickle and tangy tamarind chutney, as well as crisp bhaturas and house-made desserts.

name: PT. Gaya Prashad Shiv Charan
short_description: The oldest original paratha house established in 1872 in Paranthe Wali Gali serving deep-fried stuffed parathas with spicy curries.
long_description: Founded in 1872, PT. Gaya Prashad Shiv Charan is the historic progenitor of Old Delhi's famed Paranthe Wali Gali. Preserving its authentic no-frills ambiance with wooden wall planks and antique brass cookware, the shop crafts parathas that are shallow/deep-fried in pure desi ghee cast-iron karahis to golden crispness. Each paratha is served with unlimited spicy potato curry, sweet pumpkin (sitaphal) subzi, mint-banana chutney, and mixed pickle.

name: Babu Bhai Kabab Wale (Chitli Qabar)
short_description: Historic pre-1947 kabab institution in Chitli Qabar world-renowned for its melt-in-mouth thread-tied Sutli and Seekh Kebabs.
long_description: Founded before 1947 in the vibrant market lane of Bazar Chitli Qabar near Jama Masjid, Babu Bhai Kabab Wale is an essential pilgrimage for meat enthusiasts. Known throughout the Indian subcontinent for its unique 'Dora' or 'Sutli' kebabs, ultra-fine minced meat is seasoned with raw papaya and 20 secret spices, wound around thick iron skewers with cotton thread to hold its delicate shape over red-hot coals, and served sizzling with spicy yellow chutney and sliced onions.

long_description: Operating since 1962 on the main road in Chawri Bazar near Hauz Qazi, Shakahari Restaurant is an authentic pure vegetarian institution with over 1,500 reviews. Spanning a quiet, air-cooled dining hall with comfortable table seating, it has retained loyal generations of diners for its distinctive culinary specialties, notably Khoya Paneer simmered in condensed milk gravy, robust Dal Urad Fry Special, and hot ghee-brushed missi rotis.

name: Padam Chaat Corner
short_description: Cherished heritage chaat corner in Kinari Bazar known for 4-pani golgappe, kalmi vada, and tangy papdi chaat.
long_description: Tucked away at the intersection of Gali Baraf Wali and Kinari Bazar in Chandni Chowk, Padam Chaat Corner has delighted street food connoisseurs for decades. Unlike commercial setups, Pandit Padam prepares pure vegetarian chaats seasoned with rock salt, dry ginger (saunth), pomegranate seeds, and fresh lemon. It is celebrated for its spicy Golgappas served with four distinct flavored waters, as well as crunchy Kalmi Vada.

name: Sita Ram Pethe Wala
short_description: Historic 1951 confectioner in Khari Baoli renowned for handcrafting Agra-style pethas, kesar angoori petha, and paan petha.
long_description: Founded in 1951 along Khari Baoli Road in Naya Bans, Sita Ram Pethe Wala is Old Delhi's pre-eminent specialist in ash gourd confections (petha). Operating from a traditional brick-and-mortar storefront for over seven decades, it prepares authentic pethas made with fresh white pumpkin and pure sulfurless sugar, offering diverse textures from tender syrup-soaked Kesar Angoori to dry crystalized and betel leaf (paan) rolls.

name: Khemchand Daulat Ki Chaat
short_description: Legendary 30-year-old dessert parlour in Paranthe Wali Gali world-famous for cloud-like winter Daulat Ki Chaat and Malaiyo.
long_description: Operating for more than three decades in the heart of Chandni Chowk near Paranthe Wali Gali and Kinari Bazar, Khemchand Daulat Ki Chaat is celebrated globally for Delhi's most poetic winter culinary creation. Made through an arduous overnight process where full-cream milk and dew-chilled cream are whisked before dawn into an ethereal foam, it is served garnished with saffron strands, coarsely powdered unrefined sugar (boora), khoya crumbs, and pistachios.
